note: WAEC/NECO Biology Paper 1, round 1: full SSCE syllabus coverage - cells, nutrition, transport, respiration, excretion, reproduction, genetics, ecology, diseases, coordination, support/movement and practical skills. Numeric answers (genetic ratios, energy flow, quadrats, magnification) machine-verified.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In which organelle does aerobic respiration mainly occur?
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration releases energy in the mitochondria, the powerhouse of the cell.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which organelle contains chlorophyll in a plant cell?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll, the green photosynthetic pigment, is found inside chloroplasts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The cellulose cell wall of a plant cell mainly
questions.D: gives the cell a definite shape
questions.explanation: The rigid cellulose wall provides support and a definite shape for plant cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which structure controls all the activities of a cell?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains the genetic material and directs all cell activities.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The cell membrane is described as selectively permeable because it
questions.B: allows all substances to pass freely
questions.C: allows only certain substances to pass through
questions.D: is found only in plant cells
questions.explanation: Selectively permeable means the membrane chooses which molecules pass through.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which organelle is the site of protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes assemble amino acids into proteins during translation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of these is found in a plant cell but NOT in an animal cell?
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a large permanent vacuole; animal cells have only small temporary ones.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Lysosomes are sometimes called 'suicide bags' because they
questions.B: store food reserves for the cell
questions.C: contain enzymes that digest worn-out organelles
questions.explanation: Lysosomes hold powerful digestive enzymes that can break down cell parts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Red blood cells lack a nucleus so that they
questions.explanation: Lacking a nucleus creates space for more haemoglobin to carry oxygen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Mitosis produces daughter cells that are
questions.A: haploid and different from the parent
questions.B: genetically identical to the parent cell
questions.explanation: Mitosis copies the parent cell exactly, keeping the same diploid chromosome number.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Meiosis is important in sexual reproduction because it
questions.C: halves the chromosome number in gametes
questions.explanation: Halving the chromosome number in gametes keeps the species number constant at fertilisation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: How many chromosomes are present in a normal human sperm cell?
questions.explanation: A sperm is a gamete, so it carries half of the 46 chromosomes, which is 23.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A body cell of an organism contains 20 chromosomes. How many chromosomes will each gamete of that organism contain?
questions.explanation: Gametes are haploid, so they carry half the body-cell number of 20, which is 10.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In a flowering plant, meiosis occurs in the
questions.explanation: Pollen mother cells in the anthers and ovule mother cells undergo meiosis to form gametes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The division of the cytoplasm during cell division is called
questions.explanation: Cytokinesis is cytoplasm division; karyokinesis is nuclear division.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The raw materials for photosynthesis are
questions.explanation: Plants use carbon dioxide and water, with light energy trapped by chlorophyll.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In an experiment, a destarched leaf is tested with iodine solution and turns blue-black. This shows that the leaf contains
questions.explanation: Iodine solution turns blue-black in the presence of starch.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which class of food is the body's main source of energy?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are broken down to glucose, the chief fuel for respiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Proteins are needed in the diet mainly for
questions.B: growth and repair of body tissues
questions.explanation: Proteins supply amino acids for building new cells and repairing worn-out ones.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A child whose diet lacks vitamin D is likely to develop
questions.explanation: Vitamin D and calcium are needed for strong bones; deficiency causes rickets.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Bleeding gums and poor wound healing are classic signs of a deficiency of
questions.explanation: Vitamin C deficiency weakens connective tissue, causing scurvy with bleeding gums.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Lack of iron in the diet can lead to
questions.explanation: Iron is part of haemoglobin, so a shortage reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The enzyme that digests starch in the mouth is
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) breaks down cooked starch into maltose in the mouth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Pepsin in the stomach works best in an environment that is
questions.explanation: Pepsin is a protein-digesting enzyme that works best in the stomach's acidic juice.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Fats are digested into
questions.explanation: Lipase breaks fats (oils) down into fatty acids and glycerol.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Most digested food is absorbed into the blood through the
questions.explanation: The villi of the ileum give a huge surface area for absorption of nutrients.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Benedict's solution is used to test for the presence of
questions.explanation: On warming, Benedict's solution turns orange-red with a reducing sugar present.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The emulsion test for fats gives a
questions.explanation: Fat dissolved in ethanol forms a cloudy white emulsion when mixed with water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The association between Rhizobium bacteria and leguminous plants is an example of
questions.explanation: Both partners benefit: the bacteria fix nitrogen and receive carbohydrates, which is mutualism.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: An organism that feeds on dead and decaying matter is called a
questions.explanation: Saprophytes such as Rhizopus (bread mould) absorb nutrients from dead matter.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The xylem vessels of a plant transport
questions.explanation: Xylem carries water and dissolved mineral salts upward from the roots.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from a plant mainly through the
questions.explanation: Most water vapour escapes through the stomata of the leaves.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Translocation is the transport of
questions.explanation: Sugars made in the leaves are moved to other parts through the phloem.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The blood component that transports oxygen is
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin, the red pigment of red blood cells, combines reversibly with oxygen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which chamber of the human heart has the thickest muscular wall?
questions.explanation: The left ventricle pumps blood around the whole body, so it needs the most muscle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The pulmonary artery carries blood that is
questions.A: deoxygenated, from the body to the heart
questions.B: oxygenated, from the lungs to the heart
questions.C: oxygenated, from the heart to the body
questions.D: deoxygenated, from the heart to the lungs
questions.explanation: It is the only artery carrying deoxygenated blood, taking it to the lungs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Blood is prevented from flowing backwards in the heart by the
questions.explanation: Valves like the bicuspid and tricuspid ensure one-way flow through the heart.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The wall of a capillary is one cell thick. This adaptation
questions.C: allows rapid exchange with the tissues
questions.explanation: A thin wall shortens the diffusion distance for oxygen, food and wastes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A person with blood group O is called a universal donor because such blood
questions.B: has both antigens A and B
questions.D: has neither antigen A nor B on the red cells
questions.explanation: With no A or B antigens, group O red cells are not clumped by the recipient's antibodies.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Fibrinogen, prothrombin and platelets are all involved in
questions.explanation: These factors interact in a cascade that forms a clot sealing wounds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A farmer's crops wilt at midday even though the soil is moist. The most likely explanation is that
questions.explanation: When water loss from leaves is faster than uptake, cells lose turgor and the plant wilts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In which blood vessel is blood pressure lowest?
questions.explanation: Veins returning blood to the heart, like the vena cava, carry blood at the lowest pressure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The word equation for aerobic respiration is
questions.B: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration uses oxygen to release energy from glucose completely.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: During vigorous exercise, human muscles may respire anaerobically, producing
questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration in muscle converts glucose to lactic acid with little energy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Anaerobic respiration in yeast is used in baking because it produces
questions.C: lactic acid that makes dough rise
questions.D: carbon dioxide that makes dough rise
questions.explanation: Yeast fermentation releases carbon dioxide bubbles that raise the dough.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The organ of gaseous exchange in a fish is the
questions.explanation: Fish take dissolved oxygen from water across their gill filaments.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which feature of the alveoli speeds up gaseous exchange?
questions.C: Thin, moist walls and a rich blood supply
questions.explanation: Thin moist walls, dense capillaries and a huge surface area all favour diffusion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Limewater turns milky when exhaled air is bubbled through it. This shows that exhaled air contains
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide reacts with limewater to form a milky precipitate of calcium carbonate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Insects exchange gases directly with their tissues through the
questions.explanation: Air reaches body tissues directly through spiracles and tracheae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Compared with inhaled air, exhaled air contains
questions.B: more oxygen and less carbon dioxide
questions.C: more carbon dioxide and less oxygen
questions.explanation: Respiration uses oxygen and releases carbon dioxide, so the proportions swap.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The functional unit of the kidney is the
questions.explanation: Each kidney contains about a million nephrons, its filtering units.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Ultrafiltration of blood takes place in the
questions.A: the loop of Henle of the nephron
questions.explanation: Blood is filtered under pressure from the glomerulus into the Bowman's capsule.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Selective reabsorption in the nephron returns useful substances such as
questions.B: urea and salts to the blood
questions.C: glucose and some salts to the blood
questions.explanation: Glucose, amino acids, much salt and most water are reabsorbed into the blood.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which organ converts excess amino acids into urea?
questions.explanation: The liver deaminates excess amino acids, removing nitrogen as urea.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The hormone that controls the reabsorption of water in the kidney is
questions.explanation: ADH from the pituitary makes the tubules reabsorb more water when the blood is concentrated.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A patient with kidney failure can have their blood cleaned artificially by
questions.explanation: A dialysis machine filters waste from blood across a partially permeable membrane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of these is NOT an excretory product in mammals?
questions.explanation: Faeces is undigested food material, not a metabolic waste product of cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which excretory product leaves flowering plants mainly through the stomata?
questions.explanation: Plants lose water vapour (transpiration) and excess oxygen via the stomata.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The male part of a flower is the
questions.explanation: The stamen, made of anther and filament, produces pollen grains.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from
questions.explanation: Pollination only delivers pollen to a stigma; fertilisation comes later.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which feature is an adaptation of insect-pollinated flowers?
questions.A: Small dull petals with no scent
questions.B: Large brightly coloured petals and nectar
questions.D: Feathery stigmas hanging outside the flower
questions.explanation: Colour, scent and nectar attract insects; their pollen is sticky or spiky.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In flowering plants, fertilisation occurs when
questions.A: the pollen tube grows down the style
questions.C: the male nucleus fuses with the egg cell in the ovule
questions.explanation: Fusion of gametes inside the ovule forms the zygote; the earlier steps only prepare it.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The part of the seed that develops into the shoot is the
questions.explanation: The plumule grows into the shoot system while the radicle forms the root.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In epigeal germination, as in the bean, the
questions.B: cotyledons are carried above the soil
questions.explanation: Epi- means above: the hypocotyl lifts the cotyledons above ground.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Germination of maize, where the cotyledons remain underground, is called
questions.explanation: Hypo- means below, so the cotyledons stay below the soil surface in maize.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The testes are located outside the abdominal cavity in the scrotum because
questions.A: sperm need light in order to develop
questions.B: they need extra space to grow bigger
questions.C: they must stay close to the bladder
questions.D: sperm develop best below body temperature
questions.explanation: The slightly cooler scrotal temperature is needed for healthy sperm formation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In the human female, fertilisation normally takes place in the
questions.explanation: Sperm meets the egg in the fallopian tube (oviduct) before the zygote travels to the uterus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The placenta functions mainly to
questions.A: produce the eggs for the ovary
questions.B: protect the foetus from all diseases
questions.C: allow exchange of materials with the foetus
questions.explanation: The placenta is the exchange surface for nutrients, gases and wastes via the umbilical cord.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The amniotic fluid that surrounds a foetus mainly
questions.A: supplies oxygen to the foetal blood
questions.B: feeds the foetus with dissolved food
questions.explanation: The fluid acts as a shock absorber protecting the developing baby.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In a 28-day menstrual cycle, ovulation normally occurs around day
questions.explanation: The egg is released from the ovary about midway, around day 14 of a 28-day cycle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: After ovulation, which hormone maintains the thickened lining of the uterus?
questions.explanation: Progesterone from the corpus luteum keeps the uterine lining ready for implantation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A seed remains inactive even under suitable conditions until its dormancy is broken. Dormancy helps the plant by
questions.B: making the seed bigger than others
questions.C: doubling the food store of the seed
questions.D: timing germination to a favourable season
questions.explanation: Dormancy stops seeds from germinating when conditions for seedlings would be poor.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A tall heterozygous pea plant (Tt) is crossed with another Tt plant. What fraction of the offspring is expected to be tall?
questions.explanation: The Punnett square gives TT, Tt, Tt and tt: three of four show the dominant tallness.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: When two heterozygous organisms are crossed, the expected phenotypic ratio for a single character is
questions.explanation: Mendel's monohybrid result: three offspring show the dominant form to one recessive.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In a dihybrid cross between two heterozygous plants (RrYy × RrYy), what fraction of the offspring shows both dominant phenotypes?
questions.explanation: The classic dihybrid ratio is 9 : 3 : 3 : 1, so nine of sixteen show both dominants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The genetic make-up of an organism is its
questions.explanation: Genotype is the allele combination; phenotype is what is seen outwardly.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: An organism with two identical alleles for a character is described as
questions.explanation: Homo- means the same, as in TT or tt; heterozygous would be Tt.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In humans, the sex of a child is determined by
questions.C: the chromosome in the mother's egg
questions.D: the chromosome carried by the father's sperm
questions.explanation: The mother always gives an X; the child is XX (girl) or XY (boy) depending on the sperm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A couple are both carriers of sickle-cell anaemia (AS). What is the probability that a child of theirs has the disease (SS)?
questions.explanation: AS × AS gives AA, AS, AS and SS: only one in four is SS.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In a cross between a homozygous red-flowered plant (RR) and a homozygous white-flowered plant (rr), the F1 offspring will be
questions.explanation: Every F1 plant is Rr, and R shows complete dominance over r.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The two strands of a DNA molecule are held together by complementary base pairs in which adenine pairs with
questions.explanation: A pairs with T and C pairs with G in the DNA double helix.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which characteristic shows continuous variation in humans?
questions.explanation: Height ranges smoothly between extremes, while blood group falls into distinct classes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A man with blood group AB marries a woman with blood group O. Which blood groups can their children have?
questions.explanation: The father passes A or B and the mother passes O, so children are AO or BO only.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Haemophilia is more common in males than females because
questions.C: the gene is on the Y chromosome
questions.D: males have only one X chromosome
questions.explanation: A single recessive allele on a male's only X chromosome shows up, with no second X to mask it.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The observable appearance of an organism is called its
questions.explanation: Phenotype covers all visible traits, the result of genes plus environment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: All the organisms of different species living together and interacting in a habitat make up a
questions.explanation: A community is the collection of all populations in a habitat.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Organisms that break down dead organic matter into simpler substances are
questions.explanation: Bacteria and fungi decompose dead matter and recycle nutrients.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In the food chain grass → grasshopper → lizard → hawk, the grasshopper is a
questions.explanation: Grasshoppers eat plants, so they are primary (first-level) consumers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Green plants in an ecosystem trap 20,000 kJ of energy per square metre per year. About how much of this is available to the primary consumers?
questions.explanation: Only about 10 per cent of the energy passes to each next trophic level.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The pyramid of energy is always broadest at the bottom because
questions.D: energy is lost at each trophic level
questions.explanation: Heat losses at every level mean less energy is available higher up.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In the carbon cycle, carbon returns to the atmosphere mainly through
questions.explanation: Living things respire out CO2 and burning fuels releases it; photosynthesis removes it.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which group of bacteria converts atmospheric nitrogen into nitrates that plants can absorb?
questions.explanation: Rhizobium and free-living fixers turn nitrogen gas into usable nitrogen compounds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Denitrifying bacteria in the soil
questions.D: change nitrates back into nitrogen gas
questions.explanation: Denitrification returns nitrogen gas to the air, completing the cycle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A plant with thick succulent stems, spines instead of leaves and a thick waxy cuticle is best adapted to
questions.explanation: These are classic xerophytic features that reduce water loss.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Mangrove trees in Nigerian coastal swamps have breathing roots (pneumatophores) that
questions.D: anchor the tree in the mud
questions.explanation: The exposed roots take in air for the submerged root system in oxygen-poor mud.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which relationship is illustrated by a tapeworm living in a human intestine?
questions.explanation: The tapeworm benefits while the host is harmed, which defines parasitism.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The region of Nigeria with tall grasses, scattered drought-resistant trees and distinct wet and dry seasons is the
questions.explanation: The savanna belt has seasonal rainfall, grasses and scattered trees like shea and baobab.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A student counts 250 organisms of a species in ten 1 m² quadrats thrown at random in a 1,000 m² field. The estimated total population of the species in the field is
questions.explanation: The mean is 25 per quadrat, so 25 × 1,000 gives 25,000 organisms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which gas is mainly responsible for the enhanced greenhouse effect?
questions.explanation: Excess carbon dioxide from burning fuels traps more heat in the atmosphere.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Rain with a pH below about 5.6, caused mainly by sulphur dioxide pollution, is called
questions.explanation: Sulphur dioxide dissolves in rain to form acids; the fall in pH kills plants and fish.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: An organism's role in its community, including what it eats and where it lives, is its
questions.explanation: The niche is the full way of life of the species, not just its address.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The organism that causes malaria is transmitted by the bite of the
questions.explanation: The female Anopheles transmits the Plasmodium parasite.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Cholera is spread mainly through
questions.explanation: The cholera bacterium spreads via faeces polluting drinking water and food.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Immunity acquired when ready-made antibodies are injected is
questions.explanation: The antibodies were made elsewhere and given by injection, so it is artificial and passive.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Vaccination protects a person by stimulating the body to
questions.explanation: A weakened pathogen triggers antibody production, giving active artificial immunity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The HIV virus weakens the immune system by attacking mainly the
questions.A: the red blood cells of the body
questions.D: the liver cells of the abdomen
questions.explanation: HIV destroys helper T-cells, the coordinators of the immune response.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Antibiotics are useful in treating
questions.explanation: Antibiotics act on bacteria; viruses need antivirals or vaccines.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: An organism that carries and transmits a pathogen without suffering the disease is a
questions.explanation: Vectors like the mosquito carry the pathogen from host to host.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: River blindness in West Africa is transmitted by the
questions.explanation: Simulium blackflies breeding in fast rivers transmit the worm causing river blindness.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The central nervous system consists of the
questions.explanation: The CNS is made of the brain plus the spinal cord only.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The gap across which an impulse passes from one neuron to the next is the
questions.explanation: At the synapse a chemical transmitter carries the signal across the tiny gap.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In a simple reflex arc, the correct pathway is
questions.A: receptor → sensory neuron → relay neuron → motor neuron → effector
questions.B: receptor → motor neuron → sensory neuron → effector
questions.C: effector → sensory neuron → relay neuron → receptor
questions.D: receptor → relay neuron → sensory neuron → effector
questions.explanation: The message goes in via sensory neurons, is relayed in the spinal cord, then out via motor neurons.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The part of the eye where light is focused to form an image is the
questions.explanation: The lens focuses light onto the retina, which contains the photoreceptors.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In bright light, the iris muscles make the pupil
questions.A: constrict to reduce light entering the eye
questions.B: dilate to admit even more light
questions.explanation: Circular muscles of the iris contract, making the pupil smaller in bright light.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Accommodation of the eye for near objects involves the
questions.A: ciliary muscles contracting so the lens becomes more convex
questions.B: ciliary muscles relaxing so the lens flattens
questions.explanation: For near vision the lens becomes fatter (more convex) to focus the image on the retina.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Photoreceptors that work in dim light but do not detect colour are the
questions.explanation: Rods are sensitive in poor light; cones handle colour and detail in bright light.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The region of the retina with no photoreceptors, where the optic nerve leaves the eye, is the
questions.explanation: No image can be detected where the optic nerve exits, hence the blind spot.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In the mammalian ear, hearing occurs in the
questions.explanation: The cochlea converts vibrations into nerve impulses heard by the brain.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The semi-circular canals of the ear are concerned with
questions.explanation: Fluid movement in these canals detects the position and motion of the head.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The ear ossicles (hammer, anvil and stirrup) function to
questions.A: amplify vibrations passed to the inner ear
questions.B: equalise the air pressure in the ear
questions.C: produce the wax that traps dust
questions.D: detect the balance of the body
questions.explanation: The three small bones relay and amplify vibrations from the eardrum to the oval window.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A knee-jerk response is rapid because the pathway
questions.A: is completed in the spinal cord without the brain
questions.B: uses hormones carried in the blood
questions.explanation: Reflex arcs are short spinal pathways, so the response is immediate and automatic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Insulin lowers blood sugar level. The gland that produces it is the
questions.explanation: The islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A person whose pancreas produces too little insulin is likely to suffer from
questions.explanation: Without enough insulin, glucose cannot enter cells, so blood sugar stays dangerously high.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The hormone that prepares the body for an emergency, increasing heart rate and blood sugar, is
questions.explanation: Adrenaline from the adrenal glands produces the fight-or-flight response.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Lack of iodine in the diet causes goitre because iodine is needed to make
questions.explanation: The thyroid gland swells when it lacks the iodine needed for thyroxine production.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The growth response of a plant shoot bending towards light is called
questions.explanation: Photo- refers to light; shoots are positively phototropic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The plant hormone mainly responsible for cell elongation in shoots is
questions.explanation: Auxin produced at shoot tips promotes elongation of cells behind the tip.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Roots grow downwards in response to gravity. This response is
questions.explanation: Roots are positively geotropic, growing with the direction of gravity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares nervous and hormonal coordination?
questions.A: Nerve impulses are faster, hormones last longer
questions.B: Hormones act faster than nerve impulses
questions.explanation: Electrical nerve signals are rapid but brief; hormones are slower but give sustained effects.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The axial skeleton consists of the
questions.A: skull, vertebral column, ribs and sternum
questions.C: the bones of the arms and the legs
questions.explanation: The axial skeleton forms the central axis of the body; limbs form the appendicular part.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: How many cervical vertebrae are there in the human vertebral column?
questions.explanation: Humans have seven neck (cervical) vertebrae, twelve thoracic and five lumbar.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The vertebrae to which the ribs are attached are the
questions.explanation: The twelve thoracic vertebrae each carry a pair of ribs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The shoulder joint is an example of a
questions.explanation: The rounded head of the humerus fits into the socket of the scapula.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The elbow joint allows movement in one plane only. It is a
questions.explanation: Like a door hinge, the elbow bends and straightens in one plane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Tough cords that connect muscles to bones are called
questions.explanation: Tendons join muscle to bone; ligaments join bone to bone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Ligaments connect
questions.explanation: Ligaments strap bones together at joints, keeping them stable.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The biceps and triceps of the upper arm work as antagonistic muscles. This means that
questions.A: one contracts while the other relaxes to move the forearm
questions.B: both contract together to bend the arm
questions.C: both relax to bend the arm
questions.explanation: When the biceps bends the arm the triceps relaxes, and the reverse straightens it.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The cartilage found at the surface of bones in a joint functions to
questions.explanation: Smooth cartilage lets joint surfaces glide and cushions impacts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Red blood cells are produced in the
questions.explanation: The marrow of long bones is the main factory for red blood cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A student draws a cell 40 mm long. If the cell's actual length is 0.2 mm, the magnification of the drawing is
questions.explanation: Magnification = drawing size ÷ actual size = 40 ÷ 0.2 = 200.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A cell measured 0.05 mm across. Under a microscope magnification of ×400, the image the student sees will measure
questions.explanation: Image size = magnification × actual size = 400 × 0.05 = 20 mm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: To test a leaf for starch, the leaf is first boiled in alcohol to
questions.explanation: Decolourising in hot alcohol removes the green pigment so the iodine colour can show.
